desired_action.description: Cast a ballot in the fictional Riverbridge municipal election
desired_action.actor_group: Fictional eligible adult residents of Riverbridge
desired_action.time_horizon: During the fictional municipal election in spring 2026
desired_action.observable_success: A resident who chooses to participate casts one ballot before polls close

observed_non_action.description: Some fictional eligible residents did not cast a ballot
observed_non_action.period: The fictional Riverbridge municipal election in spring 2026

evidence.population: Fictional adult residents who considered whether to vote
evidence.sampling_method: Invented convenience sample for a software demonstration; no participants were recruited
evidence.moderator_prompt: What, if anything, made voting in the fictional local election feel worthwhile or difficult?
evidence.theme: The invented discussion contains both doubts about whether one vote affects local decisions and practical scheduling concerns.
dissenting_views: Some fictional participants value choosing between candidates even when they doubt the election's effect.
Others describe work schedules as the main obstacle rather than low perceived impact.
evidence.anonymized_quote: I am not sure one vote would change what happens.
limitations: Every participant, theme, and quotation is fictional and created only to demonstrate the schema.
A small invented focus group cannot estimate how common any view is among residents.

evidence.population: Fictional eligible adult residents invited to the demonstration survey
evidence.question: How much do you believe voting in the fictional Riverbridge municipal election can influence local decisions?
evidence.sampling_method: Invented opt-in demonstration survey; no invitations were sent and no responses were collected
limitations: All counts are invented and do not describe real residents or a real election.
The response distribution cannot establish why anyone abstained or represent a population.
